questions.q: Which phrase best summarizes the purpose of Enterprise Architecture in the TOGAF Standard?
o: To document the current IT estate for audit
To guide effective change in pursuit of the enterprise's goals
To eliminate the need for a project management office
questions.e: EA is a framework for continuous change that links strategic direction to business value, guiding effective change in pursuit of the enterprise's goals. Short form: EA aligns business and IT.

questions.q: Which architecture domain describes the logical software and hardware infrastructure capabilities and standards?
questions.e: The Technology Architecture describes the logical software and hardware infrastructure capabilities and standards, including middleware, network, platforms, and runtime environments.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognized benefit of having an Enterprise Architecture?
o: It guarantees that no project will ever fail
It reduces the risk of future investment and increases return on existing investment
It removes the need for governance
It fixes the technology stack permanently
questions.e: Benefits of EA include increasing return on existing investment, reducing the risk of future investment, better strategic decision making, and faster, cheaper procurement.

questions.q: The Enterprise Continuum is best described as which of the following?
o: A categorization for classifying and structuring re-usable architecture and solution assets
A container for the core architectural artifacts
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum is a view for classifying and structuring re-usable architecture and solution assets from generic to organization-specific.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository is the central store of the architectural representation of assets in operation across strategic, segment, and capability levels?
questions.e: The Architecture Landscape sits at the centre of the repository and holds the architectural representation of assets in operation at the strategic, segment, and capability levels.

questions.q: How is the top-level structure of the TOGAF Content Framework organized?
o: It mirrors the phases of the ADM
By the levels of the Enterprise Continuum
questions.e: The Content Framework's top-level structure mirrors the ADM phases and acts as a companion to the ADM, putting each deliverable in the context of the holistic view.

questions.q: An Architecture Capability is best understood as which of the following?
o: A single software tool for modeling
A business capability for architecture, run like any other operational unit
A catalog of solution building blocks
questions.e: An Architecture Capability is a business capability for architecture, with organization structures, roles, skills, responsibilities, and processes, run like any other operational unit.

questions.q: According to TOGAF, which is the most critical source of gaps between baseline and target?
questions.e: Gaps occur in all four domains, and ignored stakeholder concerns are the most critical source of gaps. A gap states what must change between baseline and target.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes where the Preliminary Phase and Requirements Management sit relative to the ADM cycle?
o: Both are inside the lettered A-H cycle
Preliminary precedes the cycle; Requirements Management sits at the centre
Preliminary is at the centre; Requirements Management precedes the cycle
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase precedes the eight-phase cycle (A-H), and Requirements Management sits at the centre and operates continuously.

questions.q: A team is producing an Application Portfolio Catalog and a Logical Data Diagram. In which ADM phase are they working?
questions.e: The Application Portfolio Catalog and Logical Data Diagram are Phase C artifacts, since Phase C covers both Data and Application architectures.

questions.q: Which deliverable, created and approved in Phase A, serves as the contract between the architecture team and the sponsor and defines scope and approach?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work is developed and approved in Phase A, defines scope and approach, and acts as a contract between the architecture team and sponsor.

questions.q: Interoperability conflicts between candidate solutions are consolidated and reconciled primarily in which phase?
questions.e: Interoperability is consolidated and reconciled as a step in Phase E, minimizing interoperability conflicts between the selected solutions.

questions.q: Which deliverable is created in Phase F to enable architecture governance within the implementation projects?
questions.e: The Implementation Governance Model is created in Phase F to enable architecture governance within implementation projects; it is then applied in Phase G.

questions.q: In Phase G, what is the primary role of the Architecture Contract?
o: To trigger a new ADM cycle
To be one of the simplest means of ensuring implementation conforms to the target architecture
To communicate the vision to executives
questions.e: The Architecture Contract is a joint agreement realized through governance and is one of the simplest means to ensure implementation conforms to the target architecture.

questions.q: Which artifact is the most important architectural input that triggers Phase H, Architecture Change Management?
questions.e: The Change Request is the most important architectural input to Phase H; it describes a deviation and can kick-start a further cycle of architecture work.

questions.q: According to TOGAF 10, how does developing architecture for different purposes and levels support Agile?
o: By replacing sprints with a waterfall plan
By providing governance and guardrails and identifying reusable components for shorter cycles
By removing the need for an EA capability
By mandating a single fixed backlog for the whole enterprise
questions.e: TOGAF supports the digital and Agile enterprise by managing technical debt cohesively, identifying reusable standard components for shorter cycles, and providing governance and guardrails.

questions.q: What does the requirements baseline maintained in the Requirements Management phase represent?
o: A snapshot of all agreed, reviewed, and approved requirements
questions.e: The requirements baseline is a snapshot of all agreed, reviewed, and approved requirements, maintained as the single point of truth.

questions.q: How do the ADM Techniques relate to the ADM itself?
o: They provide techniques and guidelines that support applying the ADM
They are mandatory in every phase
They are stored only in the Solutions Continuum
questions.e: The ADM Techniques document provides techniques such as principles, gap analysis, risk management, and business scenarios that support applying the ADM.

questions.q: Who approves architecture principles after they are developed?
questions.e: Architecture principles are developed by enterprise architects with key stakeholders and then approved by the Architecture Board; they are kept in a Principles Catalog.

questions.q: A commonly tested trap: the 'Implications' section of a principle describes which of the following?
o: The consequences of not following the principle
The requirements for Business and IT to carry out the principle
questions.e: Implications state the requirements, resources, costs, and activities for Business and IT to carry out the principle, not the consequences of ignoring it.

questions.q: A principle that enables good-quality, consistent, enforceable decisions even in complex or unforeseen situations satisfies which criterion?
questions.e: Robust means the principle enables good-quality, consistent, enforceable decisions even in complex situations. The five criteria are Complete, Consistent, Stable, Understandable, Robust.

questions.q: Where do the mitigations identified by the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment ultimately feed?
o: Into the Implementation and Migration Plan
questions.e: The BTRA is applied in Phase A; the risks per readiness factor are assessed and their mitigations feed into the Implementation and Migration Plan and roadmap (E/F).

questions.q: Which categories of risk does TOGAF distinguish, driven top-down from business value?
questions.e: TOGAF classifies risks by type as time (schedule), cost (budget), and scope. These map to standard project management risk categories. Initial and residual are the two risk levels, not types.

questions.q: Within a single ADM cycle, what does architecture development iteration primarily enable?
o: Capturing stakeholder concerns for the first time
Operating multiple ADM phases, such as B, C, and D, concurrently
questions.e: Architecture development iteration supports operating multiple phases concurrently, managing the interrelationships of Phases B, C, and D, which are often done together.

questions.q: Which of the following are the three levels of the Architecture Landscape?
questions.e: The three Landscape levels are Strategic, Segment, and Capability, distinguished by breadth, detail, and time horizon. Baseline/Transition/Target are states.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of architecture partitioning?
o: It guarantees a single enterprise-wide model
It enables parallelization of work across teams and clarifies responsibilities
It removes the need for governance
It forces all domains into one partition
questions.e: Partitioning enables conflict management through clear responsibilities, parallelization of work, reuse of modular segments, and reduced complexity for effective governance.

questions.q: The four purposes that frame the planning horizon, breadth, and depth of an architecture capability include which of the following?
o: Support Strategy, Portfolio, Project, and Solution Delivery
questions.e: The four purposes are Support Strategy, Support Portfolio, Support Project, and Support Solution Delivery, each with a characteristic breadth, depth, and time period.

questions.q: Why does the ADM need to be governed?
o: Because governance replaces the need for stakeholders
Because the ADM creates and maintains the EA (a change), and without governance you cannot tell whether projects move toward the target
Because governance produces the Architecture Vision
questions.e: The ADM creates, develops, and maintains the EA (a change), so it must be governed; without governance you cannot tell whether projects are moving toward the target.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the Architecture Board?
o: Granting dispensations and enforcing architecture compliance
questions.e: The Architecture Board enforces compliance, grants dispensations, monitors and controls architecture contracts, resolves conflicts, and provides an escalation capability.

questions.q: Which Architecture Contract is created at the end of Phase F with the agreed Implementation and Migration Plan and is also used in Phase H?
o: Business Users / Business Stakeholders Architecture Contract
questions.e: The Business Users / Business Stakeholders Architecture Contract is created at the end of Phase F with the agreed plan and is also used in Phase H.

questions.q: During an Architecture Compliance Review, the architect can recommend which of the following?
o: Enforce compliance, grant a temporary dispensation, or change the target
questions.e: The architect acts as auditor and advisor; recommendations are to enforce compliance, provide temporary relief (dispensation), or change the target architecture.

questions.q: In the TOGAF Standard, what is a stakeholder concern?
o: A deliverable signed off by the sponsor
An interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders that may lead to requirements
questions.e: A concern is an interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders, covering areas like performance, reliability, and security; concerns lead to requirements.

questions.q: At which point in the ADM are selected ABBs typically refined into SBBs?
questions.e: ABBs are identified in Phases A-D; selected ABBs are refined into SBBs in Phase E, where they are either purchased or developed.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Communications Plan?
o: To act as the container for core architectural artifacts
To ensure the right information reaches the right stakeholders at the right time
To define scope and approach for the cycle
To trigger a new architecture development cycle
questions.e: The Communications Plan conveys architecture information to stakeholders within a planned, managed process, ensuring the right information reaches the right people at the right time. It is created in Phase A.

questions.q: Which deliverable is an order from the sponsoring organization to the architecture team that establishes the project and triggers Phase A?
questions.e: The Request for Architecture Work is an order from the sponsoring organization to the architecture team, produced by the Preliminary Phase and used as input to Phase A.

questions.q: Which deliverable provides a high-level, aspirational summary of capabilities and business value and is an early summary of the full Architecture Definition?
questions.e: The Architecture Vision is the high-level, aspirational view of capabilities and business value, an early summary of the full Architecture Definition, created in Phase A.

questions.q: When is the first version of the Architecture Roadmap produced?
questions.e: The first version of the Architecture Roadmap is produced in Phase E, adjusted in Phase F, and used as governance input in Phase G.

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a 'draft' deliverable?
o: It has been reviewed and signed off
It is under development, with no formal review or approval yet
It is archived in the repository
It can only change via governance
questions.e: A draft deliverable is under development with no formal review or approval yet. Approved means reviewed and approved, but not necessarily finalized.

questions.q: Every ADM architecture project begins with which phase, regardless of the entry point into the ADM cycle?
questions.e: Every architecture project begins with Phase A: Architecture Vision. The Preliminary Phase establishes the capability before any cycle; phases B-H may be iterated or adapted based on the situation.

questions.q: Scope is mostly limited by which combination of factors?
o: Only the number of applications in the estate
People, finance, objectives, stakeholder concerns, and the EA team's organizational authority
Only the choice of modeling notation
Only the number of ADM phases used
questions.e: Scope is mostly limited by people, finance, objectives, stakeholder concerns, and the organizational authority of the EA team, alongside the four scope dimensions.
